title: Children for the source tax tariff
purpose: Ask employees subject to source tax about each child, following the calculator's per-child logic, to decide which children count for the tariff digit and whether a single employee gets the H tariff.

stories.title: Ask each child's age status and household, only where the tariff needs it
stories.i_want: employees subject to source tax to say whether they have children and, for each child, whether it is a minor, of age and in first education, or neither, and whether it lives in their household
stories.so_that: Lonio can decide child by child whether a child counts for the tariff code it computes, while employees not subject to source tax are not asked about their children at all
stories.priority_reason: Lonio replaces HR's manual click-through of the Zurich calculator (D-001); without the child questions no tariff code can be computed. HR today does not know up front who must answer source tax questions (F-hr_transcript-b84498).

acceptance_criteria.title: Children question only for employees subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee filling in the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio has established whether the employee is subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.then: only an employee subject to source tax is asked whether they have biological or adopted children, answered yes or no, and the answer is required; for a married employee or registered partner the question includes the children of the spouse or partner, for everyone else only the employee's own children. Employees not subject to source tax are not asked. The answer is used only for the source tax tariff code.

acceptance_criteria.title: Age status asked for each child
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers that they have children
acceptance_criteria.then: for each child the employee is asked whether the child is 'Minor', 'Of age and in first education' or 'Neither' (required); the employee can add further children and remove a child, and the child questions repeat per child. If the employee has no children, no child questions are asked.

acceptance_criteria.title: Child answers that no longer apply are not kept
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee who answered child questions
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee changes an earlier answer so that they are no longer subject to source tax, answers that they have no children, or removes a child, and then submits
acceptance_criteria.then: the child answers that no longer apply are kept while the employee goes back and forth but are discarded on submission

stories.title: Ask custody and common household for a minor child living with the employee
stories.i_want: for each minor child living in the employee's household, to know whether custody is sole or shared, and for shared custody whether the employee lives with the other parent and whether there is alternating care
stories.so_that: Lonio decides, as the calculator does, whether the child counts for the tariff code and whether it counts as an H child for a single employee
stories.priority_reason: A minor child in the household is the main child case; a wrong answer path gives a wrong tariff code, which Lonio now owns instead of HR (D-001).

acceptance_criteria.title: Custody asked for a minor child in the household
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax with a minor child
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers that the child lives in the same household
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked whether custody is 'Shared custody' or 'Sole custody' (required); this is not asked for a child outside the household or a child of age

acceptance_criteria.title: Sole custody counts the child
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax with a minor child in the household
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers 'Sole custody'
acceptance_criteria.then: no further question is asked for the child; the child counts for a married employee or registered partner and counts as an H child for a single, divorced, widowed or separated employee

acceptance_criteria.title: Shared custody result for a married employee or registered partner
acceptance_criteria.given: a married employee or registered partner subject to source tax with a minor child in the household under shared custody
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee has answered the shared-custody questions
acceptance_criteria.then: a common household with the other parent counts the child without further questions; without a common household the child does not count if there is no alternating care, or if there is alternating care and the other parent makes the larger financial contribution. With alternating care and the employee as larger contributor the result is not determined: the calculator exploration did not show this case, so Lonio cannot compute the tariff code for this employee until it is verified (see OQ-child-paths-undetermined).

stories.title: Ask custody and alternating care for a minor child not living with the employee
stories.i_want: for each minor child outside the employee's household, to know whether the employee shares custody (married or registered partner) or has parental custody (single, divorced, widowed, separated), and whether there is alternating care
stories.so_that: Lonio decides, as the calculator does, whether such a child counts for the tariff code, and counts as an H child for a single employee
stories.priority_reason: Without these answers Lonio cannot compute the tariff code for employees whose minor children live elsewhere; Lonio owns the tariff result instead of HR (D-001).

acceptance_criteria.title: Custody question depends on the civil status for source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax with a minor child that does not live in their household
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee has answered the household question
acceptance_criteria.then: a married employee or registered partner is asked whether there is shared custody, yes or no (required); a single, divorced, widowed or separated employee is instead asked whether they have parental custody, yes or no (required). Each is asked only one of the two questions.

stories.title: Ask who contributes more to the child's maintenance
stories.i_want: to know whether the employee or the other parent makes the larger financial contribution to a child's maintenance, but only where the calculator needs it
stories.so_that: Lonio can decide whether a child in alternating care, or a child of a single parent living together with the other parent, counts for the tariff code, without asking anyone else about their finances
stories.priority_reason: The answer decides whether the child counts and whether a single employee gets the H tariff; Lonio owns the tariff result (D-001). Asking it only where needed follows data minimisation (G-01).

acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked who makes the larger financial contribution to the child's maintenance: 'The employee' or 'The other parent' (required); without alternating care this question is not asked on that basis

stories.title: Ask household and maintenance for a child of age in first education
stories.i_want: for each child of age in first education, to know whether the employee lives with the other parent and, where needed, whether the employee pays more than 50% of the child's maintenance
stories.so_that: Lonio decides, as the calculator does, whether an adult child in first education counts for the tariff code and whether it counts as an H child for a single employee
stories.priority_reason: Without these answers Lonio cannot compute the tariff code for employees with children in first education; Lonio owns the tariff result instead of HR (D-001).

acceptance_criteria.title: Questions for a child of age in first education
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax with a child of age and in first education
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee has answered the household question
acceptance_criteria.then: if the child lives in the household, the employee is asked whether they live in a common household with the child's other parent (yes or no, required); the employee is asked whether they pay mainly (more than 50%) for the child's maintenance (yes or no, required) when the child lives outside the household, or in the household without a common household with the other parent

acceptance_criteria.title: Result for a married employee or registered partner
acceptance_criteria.given: a married employee or registered partner subject to source tax with a child of age in first education
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee has answered the child questions
acceptance_criteria.then: the child counts if it lives in the household with a common household with the other parent; it does not count if it lives outside the household and the employee does not pay more than 50% of its maintenance. In the other cases (outside the household and mainly maintained, or in the household without a common household with the other parent) the result is not determined: the calculator exploration did not show them, so Lonio cannot compute the tariff code for this employee until they are verified (see OQ-child-paths-undetermined).

acceptance_criteria.title: Result for a single, divorced, widowed or separated employee
acceptance_criteria.given: a single, divorced, widowed or separated employee subject to source tax with a child of age in first education
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee has answered the child questions
acceptance_criteria.then: a child in the household counts as an H child if the employee pays more than 50% of its maintenance (no common household with the other parent) or makes the larger financial contribution (common household); a child outside the household that the employee mainly maintains counts without H. In the other cases (common household with the other parent as larger contributor, or a child not mainly maintained by the employee) the result is not determined: the calculator exploration did not show them, so Lonio cannot compute the tariff code for this employee until they are verified (see OQ-child-paths-undetermined).

stories.title: Derive the child digit and the single-parent H tariff
stories.i_want: Lonio to derive the child digit of the tariff code and whether a single employee gets the H tariff from the per-child results
stories.so_that: the computed tariff code recorded for HR matches the Zurich calculator and HR no longer clicks through the calculator by hand
stories.priority_reason: HR's manual calculator step is replaced by Lonio's computed tariff code (D-001, F-hr_transcript-4e180e); a wrong digit or letter means a wrong source tax deduction.

acceptance_criteria.title: Child digit equals the number of children that count
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio computes the tariff code
acceptance_criteria.then: the child digit is the number of children that count, including H children (for example three counting children of a married employee with an employed spouse give C3Y, and one counting and one non-counting child give digit 1); with no children or none counting the digit is 0. Results with more than 3 children are verified against the calculator before go-live (see OQ-calculator-coverage). The digit is always derived again from the latest answers.

acceptance_criteria.title: H tariff for single parents with an H child
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides the tariff letter
acceptance_criteria.then: a single, divorced, widowed or separated employee gets the H tariff if at least one child counts as an H child (for example one counting child and one H child give H2); a single employee without such a child keeps tariff A; a married employee or registered partner never gets the H tariff
